For example, “Quand est-ce que tu viens?” (When are you coming?). On the other hand, “lorsque” is a bit more formal and is often used in written French or when you're narrating events. So, if you’re chatting casually or asking questions, go with “quand” for its simplicity and familiarity. If you find yourself in a more formal setting, or you’re trying to convey an idea that feels a bit more sophisticated, “lorsque” will serve you well. Ultimately, don’t stress too much! Question: Is Canada really as good as people often make it seem?
Old_Answer: I teach French as a second language to immigrants and I love to ear them talk about their experience in Canada (Quebec, to be more precise). From what I get, they usually like it a lot. They have some complains, but mostly they have no regrets. Their complains: There are many things they like, however, The Chineses talk to me about the fresh air and the worker rights. The Cubans and the Colombians talk to me about how they feel safe here (even in Montreal, which is probably the least safe city in Quebec). Most of them have kids and they say they’re happy that they get monetary aid from the government. I believe Canada is a good place to live. You can get a diploma for almost free if you stop before university. Anyhow, even after that, it is not that expensive and many people get money from the government. My boyfriend has health complications and we don’t have to spend a crazy amount of money for him to get healed. Of course, it isn’t perfect, but I feel so lucky that I was born here.
